description: The Namangan gathering took place near the city administration over methane-station queues, but the contemporaneous report says participants had not formulated demands or selected a leader to bring them to officials. A demand directed to Uzbekistan's government or policy remains unresolved.
required_followup: Seek distinct contemporaneous evidence of an explicit demand or appeal to a domestic public authority; retain pending_state_target until established.

description: The main local report is in Uzbek. It was read for this candidate, but its translation and terminology have not received independent human review.
required_followup: Obtain an independent Uzbek-language review if available; keep the source attribution and uncertainty intact.

description: Twenty-five searches and 204 source cards are saved. Broad weekly searches cover Jan. 1–7, 8–14, 15–21, and 22–31; discovery remains incomplete across local outlets, regions, sectors and month-boundary continuity. Searches include Uzbek, Russian and English paths; the candidate set remains provisional and no absence conclusion is supported.
required_followup: Continue bounded Uzbek-, Russian- and English-language searches across Jan. 1–7 and Jan. 22–31, additional regions and public-service/worker sectors; check December 2020 and February 2021 for physical episode continuity before closing this gap.

description: The latest official Mass Mobilization dataset bytes/universe and additional Coding Procedure remain unavailable under the coordinator's baseline gate; LexisNexis coverage is also absent.
required_followup: Coordinator to retain pending official baseline and method compatibility; open-web findings remain provisional.

description: The Altyaryk refinery workers' reported complaints concern layoffs, plant inactivity and wages. Eurasianet describes the Jizzakh Petroleum management venture as involving state-owned Uzbekneftegaz and Gazprom, but the captured January accounts do not show workers explicitly demanding action by Uzbekistan's government or a public policy.
required_followup: Seek direct contemporaneous evidence of the workers' addressee, any appeal to a domestic authority, and the relationship between the claimed grievance and state policy; retain pending_state_target until established.

description: The Altyaryk report headline describes hundreds, but no exact protest attendance count or independently assessed crowd evidence is captured. Workforce totals and workers said to risk job loss are not turnout.
required_followup: Locate an attributable participant count or assess contemporaneous crowd imagery if available; keep exact participant bounds null.

description: Sources describe Altyaryk workers acting repeatedly after work as of January 18-19 but do not establish a last assembly date. Repetition each workday is not proof of uninterrupted physical presence or a month-end end date.
required_followup: Search later January and February reporting for the last physical gathering and whether the same workers/action continued; document gaps without inferring a close.

description: The Labour Mission account is in Russian and the Uzbek service report was reviewed in Uzbek; neither has independent human language review recorded. Eurasianet provides English-language context but cites Ozodlik for some event details.
required_followup: Seek independent language review if available and preserve the distinct source attributions and translated uncertainty.

description: The RFE/RL retrospective confirms a January 11 road blockade by a group of women in Jizzakh over household gas and electricity interruptions but provides no attendance estimate; the 50-person criterion is unresolved.
required_followup: Find contemporaneous or otherwise attributable coverage with a protester count or suitable crowd evidence; do not infer attendance from the number of affected homes.

description: The Jizzakh women protested household gas and electricity interruptions; local authorities met with them and a coal delivery followed, supporting a domestic public-service addressee. The precise service operator and category mapping remain unclear because utility restoration is not explicitly represented in the seven available demand labels.
required_followup: Check the original coding procedure for utility/service demands and seek reporting naming the utility operator; retain the reported grievance and local authority response without assuming gas or electricity was restored.

description: The January 19 Cholish–Urgench road blockade is reported without a crowd estimate; whether 50 people assembled is unknown.
required_followup: Seek contemporaneous reporting or attributable crowd evidence; do not treat road users or the affected population as protesters.

description: The Cholish action is linked to gas/electricity shortages, but the report does not name a public authority or utility as addressee and the service grievance does not clearly map to the seven demand categories.
required_followup: Find reporting identifying the addressee, utility and any public-policy demand; consult original coding procedure before assigning a category.

description: The January 26 Ozodlik report names additional gas-related road-blocking actions in Khorezm, Bukhara, Surkhandarya, Andijan and Fergana without giving dates or attendance for each location in the captured section. These are leads, not separate dated qualifying events.
required_followup: Search each named district/city in local Uzbek and Russian reporting for exact action dates, headcounts, demand addressees and continuity; keep undated accounts out of coded January events until verified.

description: A January 2 NOVA24 article dates a Muzrabot electricity-related road action to December 27, 2020. It reports restoration of electricity but not the crowd’s physical departure or any continuation into January. The item is therefore earlier-month context, not a January event or evidence of a continuous episode.
required_followup: Check dated December 2020 and early-January reporting for the exact Muzrabot gathering and its physical end; retain the December owner if no physical continuation into January is documented.

description: Podrobno was published Dec. 29 and says video of the Kokand women’s road blockade circulated the previous day, Dec. 28; this dates video circulation, not necessarily the physical action. A closely matching UzNews account has no captured publication/event date. The physical date and crowd end are unknown, and neither account establishes presence into January; syndication/independence remains unresolved.
required_followup: Keep as earlier-month context with physical date unresolved unless reporting establishes when the gathering occurred, when it ended, or a distinct January gathering; do not use the video-circulation date as the physical date and do not count the matching pages as independent.

description: Opened Kun.uz S183, published Dec. 10, reports social-media video of Shargiron mahalla residents in Bukhara District voicing gas-supply grievances and attempting to block a street. The article gives no physical action/video date, attendance, confirmation that the road was actually blocked, or physical end; the 1,300-plus affected households are not turnout. Related Bukhara road/gas headers S161/S163/S184/S186/S187/S189/S190 remain search-only, and dependence/independence is unresolved. S077 and S185 may be separate or related. No January presence is established.
required_followup: Establish whether a physical gathering and actual road blockage occurred, its date and size, when it ended, whether it continued into January, and whether the similar publisher reports reproduce one official statement or contain independent reporting. Keep physical date and owner unresolved until evidence supports them.
